by
  have star_diagonal : ∀ {ι : Type u} {κ : Type v} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (blocks : κ → Matrix ι ι ℂ), star (Matrix.blockDiagonal blocks) = Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun k => star (blocks k)) :=
  by
    intro ι κ _ _ _ _ blocks
    ext ⟨row, blockRow⟩ ⟨column, blockColumn⟩
    by_cases h : blockRow = blockColumn
    · subst blockColumn
      simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    · have h' : blockColumn ≠ blockRow := Ne.symm h
      simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, h, h']
  have gram : ∀ {ι : Type u} {κ : Type v} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (blocks : κ → Matrix ι ι ℂ), star (Matrix.blockDiagonal blocks) * Matrix.blockDiagonal blocks = Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun k => star (blocks k) * blocks k) := by
    intro ι κ _ _ _ _ blocks
    rw [star_diagonal blocks, ← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]

  intro ι κ _ _ _ _ blocks unitary
  rw [Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff', gram blocks]
  have pointwise : (fun k => star (blocks k) * blocks k) = (1 : κ → Matrix ι ι ℂ) := by
    funext k
    exact Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff'.mp (unitary k)
  rw [pointwise, Matrix.blockDiagonal_one]

  have he : ∀ x y, p.eval (row x + col y) =
      ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (Polynomial.taylor (row x) p).coeff (i : ℕ) * col y ^ (i : ℕ) := by
    intro x y
    have hdegree : (Polynomial.taylor (row x) p).natDegree < d + 1 := by

    have hexpand := Polynomial.eval_eq_sum_range' hdegree (col y)

  let A : Matrix α (Fin (d + 1)) ℝ := fun x i => (Polynomial.taylor (row x) p).coeff (i : ℕ)
  let B : Matrix (Fin (d + 1)) β ℝ := fun i y => col y ^ (i : ℕ)
  have hF : (fun x y => p.eval (row x + col y) : Matrix α β ℝ) = A * B := by
    ext x y
    simpa only [Matrix.mul_apply, A, B] using (he x y)
  refine ⟨he, ⟨A, B, hF⟩, ?_⟩
  rw [hF]

task.question: Consider a bivariate real array F(x,y) = q(u(x) + v(y)), where q is a real polynomial of degree at most d and u, v are arbitrary real-valued functions of the row index x and column index y respectively. Prove that F factorizes as a matrix product A * B with inner dimension d+1, and conclude that the rank of F is at most d+1. Make explicit which polynomial identity provides the factorization and why only the degree of q — not the number of rows or columns — controls the inner dimension.
